title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, did not walk four cubits with his head uncovered: chapter Kol Kitvei, 118b; Kiddushin chapter 1, 31a. He was not an academy head, but led his contemporaries [דאש לבני גילו; provisional]—read “head of the kallah assembly”: chapter Haroeh, 57a. He was wealthy, as stated at the end of Horayot, 10b: he bought a small piece of land and lived comfortably. (See above, Abaye: fortune favored Rav Pappa, not Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua; this proves that Rav Pappa was wealthier.) He was Rav Pappa’s colleague. When Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua came from the academy: Eruvin 12a. He ate much, as stated in Pesachim, chapter Haishah, 89b. He erred: this is what it says there—while Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua ate one, Rav Pappa ate four …, Ravina eight; he said, “A hundred Pappas, but not one Ravina” (see his entry). He lived many years after expiring and falling ill, as stated in Bava Batra chapter 1. But the reading before us is Yosef, son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who expired … (see his entry). In Midrash Ruth: Rabbi Maysha, grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi (see his entry). In Rosh Hashanah 17a, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua fell ill. Rav Pappa said, “Prepare provisions for him”; he recovered, for they said in heaven that he did not insist on his own claims. Chuppat Eliyahu writes: Rav Huna son of Rav—a clear scribal error; it should read son of Rav Yehoshua—many angels argued in his favor, but were not accepted, until one came and said, “For whom are you arguing? Is it for this man, who never insisted on his own measure?” Immediately they released him from death to life. In Eruvin 56a: “These hills of Biri and Naresh have aged us.” In Bava Batra 101b: “Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua’s statement is an invention.” Rav Chinena son of Rav Yehoshua may be his brother, or it is a scribal error. Semag, positive commandment 67, 145b, writes that Rav Alfasi rules like Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua rather than Rav Huna, because they were later authorities. He died in year 4170 (see part 1). Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Yehoshua—it should read Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua; see above, Rav Yehudah son of Rav Yehoshua—said, “I heard it from Abaye’s lecture”: Avodah Zarah chapter 3, 43, beginning of side b; this is how it should read, R.Sh.A., Rosh and Rif. That matter in Rosh Hashanah 24b has Rav Huna bar Rav Idi—it should read bar Rav Yehoshua—“I heard it from Abaye’s lecture.” Rav Idi bar Avin the carpenter called him and Rav Pappa “youngsters.” He said to Rabbi Bibi bar Abaye, “From the truncated house.” And Rav Huna bar Chinena; Rav Chanina bar Ika. Rav Yehudah bar Chanina asked him; requires examination. Rabbi Yaakov of Nehar Pekod in his name. Rav Kahana said, “I saw Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua’s canopy”: chapter Tolin. Yuchasin writes that Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak was his colleague. Rav Nechemyah son of Rav Yehoshua; Rav Nechemyah son of Rav Yosef; Rabbi Pinchas bar Ammi; Rav Pappa his colleague; Rav Pappi. Rav, Rav Mesharshya’s father, was in his time; requires examination. Rava called him and Rav Pappa “white geese”: Gittin 73a; Ketubbot 85a. Rashi explains that because they were old he called them white geese (see what I wrote under the designation avvaz). Rava told Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, “When my rulings come before you and you see an objection, do not tear them up until you come before me …”: Bava Batra 130, end of side b. Rashi, Eruvin 26a, says he was Rava’s student. It is puzzling, then, how he said to Rava, “Do you not think so?” Eruvin 9a. Rava bar Shmuel. He reported Rav Sheshet: Yoma 70a; Eruvin 26a.
